answer: An operator running many aliases as a result pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the saffron quota and the ridge admission check. Because the counters live in the juniper ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. Submission rate is limited to 4 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole army of identities from one uplink. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
